column8: Mon 16 Nov: 3e citation (store first): a forward is the expected rate plus a premium, with Fama and Bliss's evidence; row 4 carries the plain split if 3e needs words.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; true but nuanced and hard to say in one sentence; row 1 carries the citable point.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; academic proof the premium moves with the cycle; too technical for 3e's budget.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e plain words if a clause is wanted (what the market expects plus what it charges for waiting); near twin of row 1 and H3-015.

Mon 16 Nov: 3a and aha 5, the dated premium (0.87 on 6 Nov is in NUMBERS 2 finding 1; FRED 0.8738 re-read 16 Nov); fix the use column: 0.87 is the 10-year yield's premium and 1.58 one forward ten years out, never '1-1.6 points above for her reinvestment years'; say 'a Fed model estimates' (row 8).
Mon 16 Nov: store; context that the premium on the freeze day is near its 1990-2026 average after a decade near zero; never a forecast.
Mon 16 Nov: store, supports row 15: part of the forty-year fall behind the 55.6% was a falling premium; ACM's own values unread.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a and 3e guard: any premium figure is one model's estimate, with its date; never printed as a fact.

Mon 16 Nov: 3a, why the payments are sized without reinvestment; quote re-read 16 Nov; name what was tested (5- and 10-year yields 10-20 years out, forecasts from 1986, the falling-rate era) and pair with row 12's split.

Mon 16 Nov: 3a; SEP longer-run 3.2% re-read 16 Nov; $13,906 and $25,144 are NUMBERS 8a's flat 4.0% and 3.0%; say it is the Fed's policy rate, not a Treasury yield, and bracket it, never a flat-3.2% figure not in NUMBERS.
Mon 16 Nov: store; forwards overshot only after 1981 and undershot before; approximate par-as-zero method; supports row 12, not printed.

Mon 16 Nov: 3a and aha 5, the honest form of the 55.6% (one cycle: 17.1% of starts 1962-1980, 80.1% of 1981-2010), now in NUMBERS 2 finding 1; '585 starting months', never '585 tests'; Keel arithmetic, S capped at 4.

Mon 16 Nov: 3a and aha 5, size when short: median $16,055 (NUMBERS 2 finding 1 as corrected) beside $34,555 at 1 in 20 of all windows and $45,266 worst, never 'usually small'; the 62 over $25,000 and the era medians are not in NUMBERS.
Mon 16 Nov: already applied to NUMBERS 2 finding 1; the wording rule (median when short, not across all 585) rides with row 13.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e limits and the professor's answer: the replay scales today's forwards by history's moves (A35), so the 55.6% is history's drift, not today's premium; the 0.52 ratio is not in NUMBERS.
Mon 16 Nov: would back aha 5 without the falling era, but 42.2% and 41.2% are plan-ladder figures not in NUMBERS: register them first or keep in the store.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e or a 3a clause: the term premium does not make the 55.6% an overstatement (54.7% centred on Kim-Wright's 0.87, NUMBERS 2 finding 1); the 73.3% at 1.6 points is not in NUMBERS; one premium at every horizon.
Mon 16 Nov: store; 67.2% is not in NUMBERS and rests on approximate forwards whose 1980s errors hit the zero floor; register before any use.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a and aha 5 guard: confirms NUMBERS 7's 'roughly four' three ways; 3.4 and 13 stay in the store; 585 counts starting months, not independent tries.

Mon 16 Nov: 3a and aha 5, why the 55.6% is never printed bare (about 18%-88% with four independent periods, NUMBERS 2 finding 1; Wilson intervals re-computed 16 Nov); the 13- and 585-try intervals stay in the store.
Mon 16 Nov: store or a reference for the overlap point; Hansen and Hodrick unread (no text layer), so Hakkio carries the quote.
Mon 16 Nov: same paper and point as Q6b-026, which was read further than this abstract.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a or 3e parallel for the overlap point: the 4% rule's US record is fewer than four independent 30-year tries; shares not bonds; Q61-030 and Q39-019 hold the share side.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a clause with row 32: insurers test unfavourable but not extreme conditions; that sixteen years at zero lies beyond it is Keel's reading and must be said as such.
Mon 16 Nov: store; the 2026 US standard names reinvestment as a choice and sets no rate; Q37-015 holds the same idea from ASOP 27.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a beside the 26 U.S.C. 130(d) clause: actuaries named structured settlements for reinvestment risk; cite as the 2002 edition, now superseded.

Mon 16 Nov: 3a store or one clause: the UK Test 1 accumulates surpluses and shortfalls at the risk-free rate with a 3% tolerance (re-read 16 Nov), so the ladder as written passes and the insurer adds capital; $9,046 is Keel arithmetic, not NUMBERS.

Mon 16 Nov: illustration only: $6,600 and 2.2% are not in NUMBERS and measure the ten without the extra Treasuries, so they read as the plan failing a UK test; Test 2 is a 1-in-200 one-year VaR, not a 1-point fall; TNA l.7 duration-matching risk.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a with row 27: 'fully funded at market' is the regulator's best estimate, the middle, never its safety standard; $34,369 is NUMBERS 2.
Mon 16 Nov: store; the loose end of the scale (rescue money sized above corporate yields); Q2a rows 15-16 hold the rescue itself.

Mon 16 Nov: 3a clause candidate, but ranking Regulation 126 against ASOP 22 is Keel's and they work together; use three points only (expected returns, risk-free forwards plus capital, zero) and name each backstop Laura lacks.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a beside Q2d's US record: zero is lived, not invented (Japan's call rate under 0.5% every year 1996-2024); one clause at most, the US record leads.
Mon 16 Nov: same point as Q31-029 and NUMBERS 2's 'not separate evidence'; aha 5's fix already holds the wording (never 585 beside the zero standard).
Mon 16 Nov: 3a, one sentence answering the professor: the premium pays her on bonds held and works against coupons reinvested; extends H7-012 and H3-015; the premium's size is one model's.
Mon 16 Nov: aha 5 already uses H3-067's wording for the IRS clause; this fix is applied there.
